I will keep this year simple and low-risk. I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so the most practical choice for me is still the local grain rotation: winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same land. I know this system well, it fits the climate, it uses machinery easily, and it gives me steady grain and straw. At my age, I do not want to spread myself too thin with crops that need too much hand labor or market guessing. I will put a small part of my land into spring peanut so I have some cash income and break the cereal-only pattern a little, but most of my land will stay in wheat and maize because that is what I trust most. I will use improved or hybrid seed, apply fertilizer at moderate levels instead of chasing the very highest yield, irrigate when the crop most needs it, and keep pesticide sprays limited to what is necessary. For tillage, I will plough before wheat where I want a clean seedbed, and use rotary or reduced tillage for the following crops to save labor and moisture.
